I think if you had any idea about how absurd our banking systems are you might be singing a different tune. Just consider how money is made. Most of all banks in the world currently operate on a fractional reserve system. What this means is that they only need to be able to cover, with real money, some fraction of what they lend out. In the US that figure is 10%. While it may not be immediately obvious this effectively creates money out of thin air. In fact 97% of new money in the global economy is created this way, as opposed to coming from governments.

That means when Joe deposits $100 at a bank that bank can then legally loan out $90 of that even if that $100 is all they have. If Joe comes back for his $100 it simply isn't there, which is the point of central banks (the Federal Reserve or "Fed" in the US) - they'd come save the day in case of a run on the bank. This multiplies money as Joe deposits $100 and $90 is loaned out. That $90 is deposited at another bank and then $81 is loaned out. That $81 is deposited and $73.10 is loaned out. And so on. That $100 deposit results in the creation of $1000 of new magical money.

But the catch here is that $1000 isn't actually money - it's debt. And the crazy part is that it's even more than $1000 of debt in our example. Banks not only lend out more money than they can cover, they also charge interest on those loans on top of it. That $1000 of debt might actually end up getting multiplied into several thousand dollars of debt. All based on a single modest initial "real" deposit of $100.

This is a really nasty system that I think people can plainly see is bound to explode. It generates vast amounts of debt to enrich a tiny minority of groups and individuals at the expense of pretty much everybody else. And the only way it keeps on trucking is when debt is paid off with more debt allowing banks to create even more debt and we keep on this insane exponential cycle. And when it falls apart banks begin to blame everybody but themselves for engaging in this system. It's the same story as with the mortgage crisis. Banks just don't give a fuck. They make money by lending money at everybody knowing even if the debtor ends up unable to pay that they'll get bailed out so long as the debt is big enough. Supporting the break down of this system is not playing Robin Hood, it's acting like a rational human being.
